verses.text: Then Job answered:
"Listen carefully to what I say. Let that be the comfort you give me.
Be patient while I speak, and after I have spoken, you can go on mocking me.
Am I complaining to a human being? Why shouldn't I be impatient?
Look at me and be shocked. Put your hand over your mouth.
When I think about this, I am terrified, and my body shakes.
Why do evil people go on living? They grow old and become more and more powerful.
Their children grow up around them, and they see their grandchildren.
Their homes are safe and free from fear. God does not punish them.
Their bulls never fail to breed. Their cows give birth and do not lose their calves.
They send out their little ones like a flock of lambs. Their children dance around.
They sing to the music of tambourines and harps, and they have fun with the sound of the flute.
They spend their lives in wealth and go down to the grave in peace.
Yet they say to God, 'Leave us alone! We do not want to know your ways.
Who is the Almighty, that we should serve him? What would we gain by praying to him?'
But their success is not in their own hands. I want nothing to do with the plans of the wicked.
How often is the lamp of the wicked put out? How often does disaster come on them? How often does God punish them in his anger?
How often are they like straw blown by the wind, or chaff carried away by a storm?
You say, 'God saves up their punishment for their children.' Let God punish them themselves, so they will know it.
Let them see their own ruin with their own eyes. Let them drink the anger of the Almighty.
Why should they care what happens to their families after they are dead and their time is over?
Can anyone teach God anything, since he judges even those in heaven?
One person dies while he is still strong, completely comfortable and at ease.
His body is well fed, and his bones are strong and healthy.
Another person dies with a bitter heart, never having enjoyed anything good.
But both of them lie down in the dust, and worms cover them both.
Look, I know what you are thinking, the plans you have to hurt me.
You say, 'Where is the great man's house now? Where are the tents where the wicked lived?'
Haven't you asked those who travel? Haven't you listened to their stories?
Evil people are spared on the day of disaster. They are rescued on the day of God's anger.
Who tells them to their faces what they have done wrong? Who pays them back for what they have done?
They are carried to the grave, and people keep watch over their tombs.
The soil of the valley feels soft to them. Everyone follows after them, just as countless people went before them.
So how can you comfort me with your empty words? Nothing is left of your answers but lies!"
